In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of capillary zone electro‐ phoresis as an experimental tool to provide information about protein structure and properties.
the use of the physicochemical models proposed to estimate the protein net charge, hydrodynamic radius, and their interrelation.

the use of capillary electrophoresis as an alternative to other techniques for the determination of protein net charge and size, and with the development of a theoretical framework to interpret the effects of solvent composition and pH on protein hydrodynamic size and net charge through the estimation of protein structure and amino acid sequence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the estimation of protein net charge and protein hydrodynamic radius from electrophoretic data is a difficult task and that further research is needed.
the estimation of protein net charge and protein hydrodynamic radius from experimental electrophoretically measured mobility is possible only under certain conditions.

protein hydrodynamic radius can be estimated through capillary zone electrokinetic techniques, but it is not possible to estimate protein hydrodynamic radius through capillary electrophoresis without knowing the protein net charge at the experimental pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

capillary zone electro­phoresis can be used for estimating the net charge and the hydrodynamic radius of a protein when a given protocol, a set of pK values for the charged amino acids, a set of experimental mobilities, and a protein structure file are available.
the models proposed here can be useful for the estimation of protein net charge and protein hydrodynamic radius from experimental data of electrokinetic mobility.

a better understanding of protein hydrodynamic radii and protein net charge through the proposed models is possible when the capillary electrophoretic protocol and the set of pKa of charged amino acids of the protein are known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the estimation of protein net charge from experimental mobility data and protein structure is a complex problem.
the estimation of protein net charge and radius through capillary zone mobility is not a straightforward task.
protein net charge and radius can be estimated with good precision from capillary zone electro‐phoretic data, provided that the effects of the background electrolyte are properly considered.
